title: Obama blames right-wing talk radio and Fox News for angering white people and for anti-government attitudes
text: Barack Obama is himself the source of the increase in racism and of distrust in an over-reaching federal government. He is the most divisive president in the history of the United States of America, and division will be his legacy. President Barack Obama accused right-wing talk radio and cable channels such as Fox News of angering white people in America about the economy, which he said was performing well under his administration. During his speech, Obama criticised Republicans who campaigned on stopping welfare queens and complained about makers and takers, and he referred to Mitt Romney's 47 percent comment. Their basic message is anti-government, anti-immigrant, anti-trade, and let's face it it's anti-change, Obama said, accusing them of lying in order to oppose him. What they are saying just isn't true, he said, before offering his own rebuttal of narratives from conservative media. Obama said that people had failed to recognise that he was improving the economy, cutting the deficit and cutting spending. It's the story that is broadcast every day on some cable news stations, on right wing radio it's pumped into cars and bars and VFW halls all across America and right here in Elkhart, he said. If you're hearing that story all the time, you start believing it. It's no wonder people start thinking big government is the problem. Obama argued that, because of conservative radio, white Americans believe that reverse discrimination is as serious a problem as discrimination against minorities. He said they were wrong, because black unemployment was still twice as high as white unemployment and Hispanic women earned 55 cents for every dollar earned by a white man. Obama also warned voters against listening to Trump's political argument.

title: Shake-up! McFarland pushed out of Trump's security team, offered Singapore post
text: Another one out the door. President Donald Trump's deputy national security adviser, K.T. McFarland, is expected to step down and has been offered the post of U.S. ambassador to Singapore, a U.S. official said on Sunday. It is a clear win for Trump's national security adviser, H.R. McMaster, who is overhauling the national security team he inherited from retired Lieutenant General Michael Flynn, who resigned as Trump's first national security adviser in February. McFarland, 65, is a former national security analyst for Fox News and was one of Trump's very first hires after he won the presidential election on Nov. 8. The exact date of her exit was unclear, said the U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. And the timing? News of her looming departure came less than a week after Trump threw his chief strategist, Steve Bannon, off the National Security Council at McMaster's urging. Bannon had a seat on the council's “principals committee,” which included the secretaries of state, defense and other ranking aides. Flynn was forced out on Feb. 13 over his contacts with Russia's ambassador to the United States, Sergey Kislyak, before Trump took office on Jan. 20. Who rises now? McFarland's expected exit will likely boost the status of Dina Powell, deputy national security adviser for strategy. She served in Republican President George W. Bush's State Department and advised Trump's daughter, Ivanka Trump, during Trump's transition to the presidency. Trump's White House has been riddled with infighting and palace intrigue as the president has struggled to get past a string of early stumbles.

title: Trump announces lobbying ban for campaign, transition and cabinet officials
text: Donald Trump has acted on his pledge on “Draining the Swamp” in Washington DC. Less than a week after his presidential nomination, he issued a new ruling that has caused alarm among lobbyists. In a move not previously taken by a US President, Trump declared that all officials working with his campaign, on his transition team and in his cabinet will be barred from working as DC lobbyists for 5 years, to prevent them from using their connections for personal gain. In addition, anyone who wants to work for Trump is now required to end all current connections to lobbying groups immediately or be dismissed. Trump has also moved to have the term lobbyist formally apply to all DC insiders working as “consultants” or “advisors”, on the grounds that “we all know they are lobbyists.” Long-serving Senators and lobbying groups have reacted with concern. Mitch McConnel declined to acknowledge the ban when questioned by reporters, while the National Institute for Lobbying and Ethics sought to discourage Trump by saying “This will have a chilling effect on his hiring, no doubt.” As a result of the ban, Trump will have to hire people who are not seeking to profit from hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars. This is not regarded as a loss. Supporters of President Trump's stand against DC lobbyists and career politicians are encouraged to share the report.

title: The landfill economy: coastal prawn farming and the global cycle of production and waste
text: The mode of production in which “maximizing growth and profits is the highest good” is irrational. A correspondent, Bart D. of Australia, summarised the entire global economy in three words: The Landfill Economy. Goods are manufactured, energy is consumed shipping them elsewhere, consumers buy them, and shortly afterwards they end up as garbage in a landfill. This is the definition of “economic growth”: waste, inefficiency and environmental destruction are not taken into account. Only two things are considered: maximising “growth” by any means necessary and maximising profits by any means necessary. The Landfill Economy now covers the entire planet. The circulating gyre of plastic waste the size of Texas between Hawaii and California is one modest example of the planetary trash dump that “growth” and profit produce as byproducts. The planet's oceans are a single large trash dump. Items ranging from plastic water bottles to abandoned fishing nets, radiation and containers that fell off ships are floating in even the most distant parts of the seas. Seabirds nesting on remote islands die of starvation as their stomachs fill with plastic fragments of “permanent growth.” Globalization has turned the planet's land masses and rivers into trash dumps. One example is coastal prawn farming. To make a quick profit along a tropical sea coast, operators dig large holes near the coast, add baby prawns, feed and chemicals to suppress algae blooms and diseases, and then harvest the prawns for shipment to the high-demand markets of the developed world.

title: Government surveillance program using hidden microphones in public spaces revealed in Bay Area
text: A government surveillance program that used hidden microphones in public places around the Bay Area has been revealed. Conversations between people standing at a bus stop can be recorded without their knowledge. This happens regularly, and the FBI does not need a warrant to do it. Federal agents are placing microphones to record conversations covertly. Jeff Harp, a KPIX 5 security analyst and former FBI special agent, said: They put microphones under rocks, they put microphones in trees, they plant microphones in equipment. I mean, there's microphones that are planted in places that people don't think about, because that's the intent. Between March 2010 and January 2011, FBI agents hid microphones inside light fixtures and at a bus stop outside the Oakland Courthouse, without a warrant, to record conversations. Federal authorities are seeking to prove that real estate investors in San Mateo and Alameda counties are guilty of bid rigging and fraud, and used these recordings as evidence. Harp said: An agent can't just go out and grab a recording device and plant it somewhere without authorization from a supervisor or special agent in charge. The lawyer for one of the accused real estate investors, who will ask the judge to exclude the recordings, told KPIX 5 News: Speaking in a public place does not mean that the individual has no reasonable expectation of privacy private communication in a public place qualifies as a protected oral communication and therefore may not be intercepted without judicial authorization. Harp said that people intending to conduct criminal activity should do so in the privacy of their own homes.

title: Hillary Clinton responds to Trump's nickname for her
text: Hillary Clinton says she is not affected by the latest nickname given to her by Republican presidential front runner Donald Trump. Appearing on ABC's This Week, the Democratic candidate was asked about Trump calling her Crooked Hillary. He can say whatever he wants to say about me, I really couldn't care less, Clinton said on ABC's This Week With George Stephanopoulos. I don't respond to Donald Trump and his string of insults about me. Clinton went on to explain why she is not concerned about Trump's insults but is willing to confront him directly. I can take care of myself, Clinton said when asked to respond to Trump's remark. What I'm concerned about is how he goes after everybody else. He goes after women. He goes after Muslims. He goes after immigrants. He goes after people with disabilities. He is hurting our unity at home. He is undermining the values that we stand for in New York and across America. And he's hurting us around the world. Trump is seeking media attention regarding Clinton at the same time as he is engaged in a contest for delegates with Senator Ted Cruz. Trump has repeatedly been outperformed at state delegate events where Cruz has organised to secure delegates ahead of the Republican Convention in Cleveland. Trump faces the possibility of losing the nomination, despite holding a large lead over Cruz, because he may have difficulty reaching the 1,237 delegates needed to win the Republican nomination. Even if he succeeds, polling indicates that Trump faces a very difficult election if he runs against Clinton.

title: Judge who jailed Kim Davis has previously ordered training on homosexuality in schools
text: The judge in the Kim Davis case is another judge denying First Amendment rights to Americans. Of note is that the 6th Circuit Court of Appeals reversed one of Bunning's decisions. The federal judge who held Rowan County Clerk Kim Davis in contempt and ordered her to jail for refusing to sign marriage licenses has on two occasions denied Christian students in Kentucky public schools their First Amendment rights by ordering them to undergo re-education training promoting the homosexual lifestyle despite their religious objections. In 2003, Federal District Judge David Bunning ordered Boyd County education officials to implement training that required school staff and students to undergo diversity education devoted principally to issues of sexual orientation and gender harassment. A number of students objected to being required to watch a propaganda video that described Christian views opposing homosexuality as wrong and presented homosexuality as a safe, healthy and fixed lifestyle that cannot be changed. When it emerged that students would be punished if they did not undergo the training, their parents brought in the Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) legal organization, which sued the Boyd County Board of Education. In 2006, the judge again sought to require Christian students to watch a propaganda video promoting the homosexual lifestyle, and denied them the ability to opt out of the training. Bunning ruled that an opt-out was unnecessary because the training did not mean that students would have to change their religious beliefs. Bunning's decision was overturned in October 2007 by the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals.

title: Mannequin Challenge goes unnoticed at Southern Rail
text: Workers who appeared to be motionless attracted no attention at Southern Rail headquarters. Customer Service Manager Simon Williams, who is usually available at short notice, told a reporter, “Everyone in the department was stock still, and I wandered amount them filming with my smartphone. “I was amazed at their ability to remain totally motionless and unfocused on other stimuli. I even filmed the maintenance people outside, tools in hand, completely immobile. “After filming for a record-breaking twenty-five minutes, I realised I'd forgotten to actually send out the email telling people to prepare for the Mannequin Challenge. “I was the only person in the building doing any activity, even if it was just dicking around because of a YouTube craze. “I've never felt so alone; it was like waiting for something I knew wasn't going to arrive, if you can imagine such a thing.” In recent weeks, the Internet trend known as the Mannequin Challenge has spread to offices and gyms across the UK. Participants hold a pose in the manner of shop mannequins and are filmed, giving the impression that a single moment has been captured on film. Whether this should be considered a challenge, or a positive development, remains under discussion. Mr Williams continued, “I've seen many videos of our passengers standing motionless on cold station platforms, but curiously that was before anyone had conceived of the Mannequin Challenge. Strange.”

title: Stunning: nearly four-fifths of white evangelicals are lining up behind Trump!
text: Multiple marriages. Little piety. Flip-flops on the issues they care about most. And still nearly four-fifths of white evangelical voters plan to cast their ballots for Donald J. Trump, a new poll has found. How? Mr. Trump's support among white evangelicals is even stronger than Mitt Romney's was four years ago as the previous Republican nominee for president, according to the poll of religious voters released on Tuesday by the Pew Research Center. White evangelicals are a prized bloc of registered voters who, when fired up, can turn out the vote through their churches and social networks. It had been unclear whether Mr. Trump could capture this core Republican constituency, because some leading evangelicals have said they are disturbed by his habit of boasting about himself and belittling others, his pledges to deport Mexican immigrants and bar Muslims from entering the country, and his past support for abortion rights and gay rights. Some influential evangelical leaders have joined the “Never Trump” camp, while others have pledged their support for Mr. Trump. More jumped aboard after he wooed about 1, 000 of them at a meeting in New York. “Trump is not a true believer in any sense, both religiously and on the issues, but he's speaking to them,” said J. Tobin Grant, a professor of political science at Southern Illinois and a columnist at the Religion News Service. “He's actively courting them, and that's what the activists want. They want to have a seat at the table, and they felt they didn't have that with Romney.” A seat at the table. That is what it comes down to. The poll also found that Roman Catholics favored Hillary Clinton, the presumptive Democratic nominee, over Mr. Trump.

title: Handcuffed at the Airport! Dissident Uzbek Writer Jailed the Moment He Came Home From Exile
text: So much for the new Uzbekistan! The first prominent dissident to return to the country since the death of its long-time leader was detained the moment he arrived on Wednesday, his wife said – a shocking blow to the new president’s efforts to change the country’s image. Uzbek police hauled writer Nurulloh Muhammad Raufkhon away in handcuffs after he landed at Tashkent airport, and threw him in jail after questioning, a tearful Gulnara Otakhonova said. Officers told her to bring him clothes and a lawyer – but would not say what he was charged with! The interior ministry in the mainly Muslim ex-Soviet state bordering Afghanistan did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Raufkhon had lived in self-imposed exile in Turkey since 2016, when he was put on a security blacklist for publishing a book that criticized former leader Islam Karimov. Karimov, blamed by Western governments for systematic human rights violations during his 25 years in power, died last September. His successor, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has tried to paint himself as a more liberal leader. And this month Raufkhon said in an interview that, despite some misgivings, he would soon return home. Was he betrayed? In an open letter to Mirziyoyev last week, Raufkhon said his safe return would suit the country “the country which is repackaging itself in front of the world community as free and fair since you came to power”. A better image for Tashkent could help Mirziyoyev forge closer ties with the West and attract foreign investment to modernize an economy that has struggled to create enough jobs, driving millions of Uzbeks to look for work abroad. Raufkhon’s wife said by telephone that she and their son waited for hours at the airport – only to see Raufkhon marched outside in handcuffs and taken to a police station.

title: Dan Pfeiffer Lets Loose on His Way Out: How the White House Lost Its Illusions and Learned to Be Liberal
text: He has finally said it out loud! Dan Pfeiffer, who quit as senior adviser at the White House last week after working with Barack Obama since his first presidential campaign, has wrestled from day one with the glaring contradiction at the heart of Obama’s public persona: he ran as the man who could end partisan polarization – yet he has presided over even more of it, despite delivering most of the substantive agenda he promised. And finally, the news media has changed so that people choose only sources that confirm what they already believe. Sound familiar?

title: Bad News for Trump! Court Blow to Ex-AIG Boss Greenberg Raises the Stakes in Trump University Fight
text: This could hurt Trump! A ruling by New York’s highest court in a fraud case against former American International Group Inc Chief Executive Maurice “Hank” Greenberg could hit the state’s case against Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump and his defunct Trump University. On Thursday the New York Court of Appeals ruled that state Attorney General Eric Schneiderman could try to claw back millions of dollars in bonus payments to Greenberg using the legal remedy called disgorgement. Unlike damages, which compensate victims’ losses, disgorgement forces a defendant to hand back gains obtained by unlawful means. The upshot? Schneiderman can go after the $5 million he says Trump personally pocketed from the Trump University real-estate seminar venture. “It doesn’t help him,” admitted Jeffrey Goldman, Trump’s lawyer in the New York case, on Monday of the Greenberg ruling. But Goldman insisted Trump expected to win and could also try to limit the amount subject to disgorgement, for example by arguing that most of it was earned outside New York. According to the state’s 2013 lawsuit against Trump, filed in state court in Manhattan, Trump University was an unlicensed, illegal operation that bilked students of up to $35,000 each between 2005 and 2011. Two proposed class actions in California make similar charges. Trump, the presumptive Republican presidential nominee, has repeatedly raised the Trump University litigation on the campaign trail, blasting the lawsuits as baseless and politically motivated. He has even accused the federal judge overseeing the California lawsuits of being biased against him because of his ethnicity. The judge was born in Indiana to Mexican parents. In the Greenberg case, the state accused the former CEO of orchestrating sham transactions at AIG and misleading shareholders about the company’s financial health between 2000 and 2005.

title: Yahoo asks US government to clarify alleged order to scan emails; ACLU files motion
text: Yahoo has asked the US government to disclose national security orders that Washington allegedly issued to obtain user data. The request follows a news report stating that Yahoo built a software program to search customers' emails for specific US intelligence. The letter to Director of National Intelligence (DNI) James Clapper was released on Yahoo's website on Wednesday. "We urge your office to consider the following actions to provide clarity on the matter: confirm whether an order, as described in these media reports, was issued; declassify in whole or in part such order, if it exists; and make a sufficiently detailed public and contextual comment to clarify the alleged facts and circumstances," the letter read. The company asked for an explanation of "under what set of circumstances" the US authorities obtained users' private information. "Citizens in a democracy require such information to understand and debate the appropriateness of such authorities and how the government employs them." According to Yahoo, the report "set a stronger precedent of transparency for our users and all citizens who could be affected by government requests for user data. As we've said before, recent press reports have been misleading; the mail scanning described in the article does not exist on our systems." Timothy Barrett, a spokesman for Clapper's office, confirmed that the DNI head had received a letter and "will respond to Yahoo directly." The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) has made a similar request to the US government. The group filed a motion with the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) requesting the release of court records.

title: Plunged Into Darkness! Power Crews Race to Puerto Rico After Maria Wrecks Its Grid
text: An entire island in the dark! Utility crews from the U.S. mainland were racing to Puerto Rico on Thursday after Hurricane Maria knocked out power to nearly the whole U.S. territory, and many of its Caribbean neighbors, officials said. The Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority (PREPA) reported that almost 100 percent of its 1.5 million customers had no power as of late Wednesday, the U.S. Department of Energy said in a Thursday update on the hurricane’s impact, after Maria’s winds snapped trees and utility poles. Puerto Rico Governor Ricardo Rossello said PREPA had been hit so hard that it could be months before electricity is restored to all those customers. Months! President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Hurricane Maria had totally obliterated the U.S. island territory of Puerto Rico, its electrical grid destroyed. In the U.S. Virgin Islands, most of the 25,000 customers on St. Croix were also without power, the DOE report added. Energy support crews have been sent to St. Thomas and St. Croix to back up Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) teams there, and others are ready to deploy to Puerto Rico as soon as conditions allow, the DOE said. The American Public Power Association said it was also rushing in utility and contractor crews from parts of the U.S. mainland to help with recovery. At least one support team is already in Puerto Rico, said Mike Hyland, senior vice president, engineering services at the association, in a phone interview. “They’ve been in San Juan since Maria passed and I believe they’re going today to St. Thomas. ... Right now our mission is to get the lights back on,” he said. But how fast can help arrive? He added that only limited flights and barges were serving the islands.

text: Hillary Clinton could be the greater evil in the presidential election even if everything printed this year about Donald J. Trump were 100% true, a commentary argued. One of the two main candidates has repeatedly, and irrationally, sought to provoke hostilities against nuclear-armed Russia as part of an unstated agenda, the same agenda that has been destroying the Middle East for decades, he wrote. The author said the central question in the current debate is whether a nuclear holocaust counts as “evil.” He said American voters, as purchasers of a product, have a right to know how much lesser this “evil” actually is compared with the name brand. He compared the choice to seasonal Cadbury Cream Eggs, a familiar product returned to the shelves: the lesser evil, with more fat and toxins this year than ever. Many Americans say they want this repackaged, re-branded item every four years, it is the only thing they want or care about politically, and they criticize those who refuse to purchase it, he wrote. He likened the process to a Black Friday crowd at Walmart that television describes as “democracy.” He said it is not democracy but oligarchy with bread and circuses. According to the commentary, the so-called “lesser evil” philosophy is the only political philosophy these voters appear to understand, while its core is overlooked: their chosen candidate will, by their own admission, commit evil acts. He said self-deception is intrinsic to supporting this fragile arrangement. He proposed changing the phrase to “evil but possibly lesser,” which he called more accurate, so that the public might consider it when each November arrives.

title: Facebook's week of trending news errors ends with 9/11 conspiracy story
text: Today is a day of remembrance for the lives lost 15 years ago at the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and on United Flight 93, and for the sacrifices made since then. Social media has been tracking 9/11 topics for the last several days, as is appropriate. Two days ago, however, Facebook also featured a story based on a truther conspiracy theory in its trending topics sidebar. 9/11 truthers are conspiracy theorists who state that the attacks were an inside job. The story came from a U.K. tabloid site called The Daily Star, and it states: “Engineers Steven Jones, Robert Korol, Anthony Szamboti and Ted Walter are part of the growing community of experts who say evidence indicates the towers were brought down in a controlled demolition. They wrote a paper for Europhysics News highlighting four important pieces of evidence pointing to this conclusion. These were: fires are not normally hot enough to heat a massive steel structure enough for it to collapse; the majority of high rise buildings have sprinkler systems that prevent a fire from getting hot enough to heat steel to a critical level; skyskrapers (sic) are protected using flame-proof materials and they are also designed so that if compromised, they do not collapse.” Apart from the spelling errors, there is a large body of evidence showing that the Twin Towers did not have adequate fireproofing on their superstructures. In addition, these four engineers are well-known truthers who disregard actual science and fact. The author does not consider them experts who must be taken seriously. That, however, is not the main issue. Facebook recently removed all of the trained journalists from its trending section.

title: Clinton’s Big Bear Hug of Obama Could Come Back to Haunt Her
text: What a turnaround! Hillary Clinton has kept her distance from President Barack Obama on a string of high-profile issues since launching her bid for the White House. Now, with left-wing challenger Bernie Sanders breathing down her neck, she is embracing Obama and his legacy with fervor. It is a risky bet. That strategy could backfire on Clinton in the long run, as Republicans hunt for ammunition to paint her as Obama’s third term should she win the Democratic nomination. Facing an unexpected challenge from Sanders in the early voting states, Clinton is casting herself as the heir to Obama’s policies to court young voters and progressives who make up the president’s political base. But is she setting herself up for trouble with a general electorate fed up with the status quo? Again and again during a tense Democratic presidential debate on Sunday, Clinton, who served as Obama’s secretary of state for four years, played up her ties to the president and accused Sanders of undermining him. Gone was any mention of her differences with the president over Syria, trade and immigration. Instead, Clinton praised the Affordable Care Act, Obama’s signature healthcare law. She trumpeted her connection to the administration’s Iran nuclear deal and lauded the White House for sending staff to Silicon Valley to discuss cybersecurity. Clinton, who ran against Obama for the 2008 Democratic nomination and then joined his administration, said she could take Sanders’ attacks on her campaign donations – one of the Vermont senator’s favorite lines – but would not tolerate the same attacks aimed at her former boss. “The comments that Senator Sanders has made ... don’t just affect me, I can take that, but he’s criticized President Obama for taking donations from Wall Street.”

title: Radio host says New York attacker entered U.S. under Schumer-backed Diversity Visa program
text: Radio host Mark Levin reported on his show tonight that the Muslim terrorist who killed 9 people in Manhattan and injured dozens entered the United States through the Diversity Visa program. The program was approved by New York Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer. On October 31, 2017, a Twitter user summarized Levin’s report: “NYC muslim terrorist came to US under Diversity VISA Program a bizarre lottery to shove more foreigners down our throats”. According to ABC 7, authorities say the man came to the United States seven years ago from Uzbekistan under the Diversity Visa Program, which offers a lottery for people from countries with few immigrants in America. On May 1, 2017, the Washington Post published an article critical of President Trump, at a time when millions were concerned that this could be the last year of the Diversity Lottery. According to the Washington Post, the lottery's premise is simple. Each year, the Diversity Visa Lottery, as it is officially known, provides up to 50,000 randomly selected foreigners, fewer than 1 percent of those who enter the drawing, with permanent residency in the United States. It is not connected to employment or family members in the United States. The only requirement is that entrants be adults with a high school diploma or two years of work experience. Winners can bring spouses and children. Citizens of countries that have sent 50,000 people to the United States in the past five years, such as Canada, China, India, Nigeria and Mexico, are ineligible to participate. The current lottery coincides with an intense debate over immigration and comes amid policy changes that have made the country less welcoming to new arrivals. President Trump has cracked down on illegal immigration and moved forward with plans to build a wall along the border with Mexico.
